lines.text: Lesson three: trading pairs. What does BTC/USDT really mean? Let's find out.
lines.say: Lesson three: trading pairs. What does B-T-C U-S-D-T really mean? Let's find out.

lines.text: Look at a shop price tag. Rice: ₹60 for one kilo.
lines.say: Look at a shop price tag. Rice: sixty rupees for one kilo.

lines.text: It compares two things: an amount of money, and one unit of the item.
lines.say: It compares two things: an amount of money, and one unit of the item.

lines.text: A crypto price works the same way: 60,000 USDT for one BTC.
lines.say: A crypto price works the same way: sixty thousand U-S-D-T for one B-T-C.

lines.text: A trading pair tells you which asset is being priced against another.
lines.say: A trading pair tells you which asset is being priced against another.

lines.text: The first half, BTC, is the base asset: the thing you buy or sell.
lines.say: The first half, B-T-C, is the base asset: the thing you buy or sell.

lines.text: The second half, USDT, is the quote asset: what the price is counted in.
lines.say: The second half, U-S-D-T, is the quote asset: what the price is counted in.

lines.text: So BTC/USDT means: the price of one BTC, in USDT.
lines.say: So B-T-C U-S-D-T means: the price of one B-T-C, in U-S-D-T.

lines.text: A symbol is the short name for a pair. Many apps drop the slash: BTCUSDT.
lines.say: A symbol is the short name for a pair. Many apps drop the slash: B-T-C U-S-D-T.

lines.text: BTC/USDT and BTCUSDT are the same pair. ETHUSDT is ETH priced in USDT.
lines.say: B-T-C slash U-S-D-T, and B-T-C U-S-D-T written as one word, are the same pair. E-T-H U-S-D-T is E-T-H priced in U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Read the price as: one BTC costs 60,000 USDT.
lines.say: Read the price as: one B-T-C costs sixty thousand U-S-D-T.

lines.text: USDT is a stablecoin: a token designed to stay close to one US dollar.
lines.say: U-S-D-T is a stablecoin: a token designed to stay close to one US dollar.

lines.text: BTC's price swings a lot. USDT's price is designed to barely move.
lines.say: B-T-C's price swings a lot. U-S-D-T's price is designed to barely move.

lines.text: That makes it a handy measuring stick for prices. But designed to stay is not guaranteed.
lines.say: That makes it a handy measuring stick for prices. But designed to stay is not guaranteed.

lines.text: Quantity is how much of the base asset you buy or sell.
lines.say: Quantity is how much of the base asset you buy or sell.

lines.text: Think of one BTC as a big block, cut into 1,000 small pieces.
lines.say: Think of one B-T-C as a big block, cut into one thousand small pieces.

lines.text: One piece is 0.001 BTC. At 60,000 USDT per BTC, it's worth just 60 USDT.
lines.say: One piece is zero point zero zero one B-T-C. At sixty thousand U-S-D-T per B-T-C, it's worth just sixty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: The price per BTC stays the same.
lines.say: The price per B-T-C stays the same.

lines.text: Notional value is the total worth of a quantity, counted in the quote asset.
lines.say: Notional value is the total worth of a quantity, counted in the quote asset.

lines.text: The formula: value in USDT equals BTC amount times USDT per BTC.
lines.say: The formula: value in U-S-D-T equals B-T-C amount times U-S-D-T per B-T-C.

lines.text: Say you buy 0.05 BTC at 60,000 USDT per BTC. 0.05 times 60,000 is 3,000 USDT.
lines.say: Say you buy zero point zero five B-T-C at sixty thousand U-S-D-T per B-T-C. Zero point zero five times sixty thousand is three thousand U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Now let the price move, and watch two orders: 1 BTC and 0.001 BTC.
lines.say: Now let the price move, and watch two orders: one B-T-C and zero point zero zero one B-T-C.

lines.text: BTC rises to 63,000. 1 BTC is now worth 63,000 USDT. 0.001 BTC: 63 USDT.
lines.say: B-T-C rises to sixty-three thousand. One B-T-C is now worth sixty-three thousand U-S-D-T. Zero point zero zero one B-T-C: sixty-three U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Both rose 5 percent. In USDT, that's 3,000 more versus just 3 more.
lines.say: Both rose five percent. In U-S-D-T, that's three thousand more versus just three more.

lines.text: If BTC falls to 57,000, they're worth 57,000 and 57 USDT.
lines.say: If B-T-C falls to fifty-seven thousand, they're worth fifty-seven thousand and fifty-seven U-S-D-T.

lines.text: A common mistake: BTC costs 60,000 USDT, so I need 60,000 USDT to trade it.
lines.say: A common mistake: B-T-C costs sixty thousand U-S-D-T, so I need sixty thousand U-S-D-T to trade it.

lines.text: No. 60,000 is the price of one whole BTC, not the size of your order.
lines.say: No. Sixty thousand is the price of one whole B-T-C, not the size of your order.

lines.text: You choose the quantity. 0.001 BTC at 60,000 costs 60 USDT, before fees.
lines.say: You choose the quantity. Zero point zero zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand costs sixty U-S-D-T, before fees.

lines.text: Your turn. Quantity: 0.02 BTC. Price: 65,000 USDT per BTC. What's the notional value?
lines.say: Your turn. Quantity: zero point zero two B-T-C. Price: sixty-five thousand U-S-D-T per B-T-C. What's the notional value?

lines.text: 0.02 times 65,000 is 1,300 USDT. Well done if you got it.
lines.say: Zero point zero two times sixty-five thousand is one thousand three hundred U-S-D-T. Well done if you got it.

lines.text: Other pairs work the same way. ETH/USDT: one ETH costs 3,000 USDT.
lines.say: Other pairs work the same way. E-T-H U-S-D-T: one E-T-H costs three thousand U-S-D-T.

lines.text: The quote doesn't have to be USDT. In ETH/BTC, the price is counted in BTC.
lines.say: The quote doesn't have to be U-S-D-T. In E-T-H B-T-C, the price is counted in B-T-C.

lines.text: ETH/BTC at 0.05 means one ETH costs 0.05 BTC.
lines.say: E-T-H B-T-C at zero point zero five means one E-T-H costs zero point zero five B-T-C.

lines.text: Before you go further: stablecoins have risks too.
lines.say: Before you go further: stablecoins have risks too.

lines.text: A stablecoin is not guaranteed to stay at one dollar. It can slip, and that's called losing its peg.
lines.say: A stablecoin is not guaranteed to stay at one dollar. It can slip, and that's called losing its peg.

lines.text: It depends on the company behind it, and on the money it holds in reserve.
lines.say: It depends on the company behind it, and on the money it holds in reserve.

lines.text: And notional value isn't profit. It's just what your BTC is worth right now.
lines.say: And notional value isn't profit. It's just what your B-T-C is worth right now.

lines.text: Let's recap. A pair prices the base asset in the quote asset: USDT per one BTC.
lines.say: Let's recap. A pair prices the base asset in the quote asset: U-S-D-T per one B-T-C.

lines.text: Value in USDT equals BTC amount times USDT per BTC.
lines.say: Value in U-S-D-T equals B-T-C amount times U-S-D-T per B-T-C.

lines.text: USDT is a stablecoin. It aims for one dollar, but that's not guaranteed.
lines.say: U-S-D-T is a stablecoin. It aims for one dollar, but that's not guaranteed.

lines.text: Check yourself: you buy 0.01 BTC at 60,000 USDT. What's the notional value?
lines.say: Check yourself: you buy zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand U-S-D-T. What's the notional value?

lines.text: 0.01 times 60,000 is 600 USDT.
lines.say: Zero point zero one times sixty thousand is six hundred U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Well done! Next up: what does an exchange do? See you in lesson four.
lines.say: Well done! Next up: what does an exchange do? See you in lesson four.
